policy_presence.summary: The University of Edinburgh does not ban the use of generative AI by students, though its use is restricted for much assessed work and governed by course-level guidance.

ai_disclosure.summary: Students must acknowledge permitted use of generative AI before submitting assessed work, providing a brief statement at the end of the submission in accordance with course instructions. Postgraduate research students who choose to use generative AI for aspects of assessed research (such as doctoral theses, MScR dissertations, or annual review submissions) should include a brief acknowledgment in the Declaration of Own Work at the start of the thesis or submission. At the University of Edinburgh, staff must be transparent about generative AI assistance, never claim AI output as their own original work, and always verify accuracy and appropriateness.

coursework.summary: The University of Edinburgh does not ban the use of generative AI by students, though its use is restricted for much assessed work and governed by course-level guidance. GenAI permissions at Edinburgh are set at assessment and course level; restrictions should be stated in the assessment task and students must consult their Course Organiser when unclear.

exams.summary: Reviewed guidance identifies misconduct in assessed work and requires course-level instructions. A separate exam-specific AI permission rule was not established in this review.

privacy_data_entry.summary: University staff are strictly prohibited from uploading personal data or confidential university information to external AI tools, and must assume third-party providers share inputs externally. Staff and researchers must not input identifiable patient/clinical data or any identifiable research participant data into any AI platform, including the University's institutional ELM platform.

academic_integrity.summary: At the University of Edinburgh, presenting AI outputs as your own original work, machine-translating assessed work to English, submitting AI content without acknowledgment, and using AI agents within university learning platforms constitute academic misconduct. An appeal cannot be lodged until the Board of Examiners or decision-maker publishes its final decision in EUCLID Student View (as results on LEARN may not yet be ratified or moderated); appeals against academic decisions must be submitted promptly within 10 working days of the result being issued for undergraduate non-final years, and within 30 working days of the result being issued for undergraduate final year and all postgraduate taught and research students. Appeals against decisions of Student Discipline Officers or the Student Discipline Committee, and appeals against decisions of Fitness to Practise Panels, must be submitted within 10 working days of the receipt of the decision. Late appeals will only be considered in extraordinary circumstances explaining and evidencing why the deadline could not be met; appeals submitted over one year after the ratified or publication date of the original decision will not be considered under any circumstances.

approved_tools.summary: ELM (Edinburgh access to Language Models) is the University of Edinburgh's AI innovation platform and a central gateway providing safer access to generative AI through large language models. The University of Edinburgh provides access to the Copilot chat service within Edge by signing in with University credentials, while full Microsoft 365 Copilot Office suite integration licenses are not currently provided. The University of Edinburgh encourages students to use ELM over external commercial AI platforms because its guidance states that data is not retained by third-party services to train models or for other purposes. March 2026 student guidance describes ELM as free to staff and students; another published entitlement page states discretionary School approval. Whether that approval condition still applies universally is not established by these sources. The full Microsoft 365 Copilot suite is not provided under the University's current institutional license agreement, and ISG currently has no plans to make the full Copilot for MS365 license available, though free Copilot chat within Edge is supported.

named_ai_services.summary: ELM is the University gateway to generative AI and Llama is listed within ELM. Copilot chat within Edge is available with University credentials; full Microsoft 365 Copilot integration is not provided. Service access does not establish assessment permission.

teaching_guidance.summary: GenAI permissions at Edinburgh are set at assessment and course level; restrictions should be stated in the assessment task and students must consult their Course Organiser when unclear. The University of Edinburgh advises staff not to rely on AI detection tools to confirm authorship, as they misclassify human and AI content and there is no reliable automated provenance method.

research_guidance.summary: The University of Edinburgh does not ban generative AI in postgraduate research, but its use is restricted for assessed work; researchers should consult supervisors and programme-level guidelines, should include a brief acknowledgment in the Declaration of Own Work if using AI for assessed research, and must adhere to publisher and funder rules. Postgraduate research students who choose to use generative AI for aspects of assessed research (such as doctoral theses, MScR dissertations, or annual review submissions) should include a brief acknowledgment in the Declaration of Own Work at the start of the thesis or submission. Staff and researchers must not input identifiable patient/clinical data or any identifiable research participant data into any AI platform, including the University's institutional ELM platform.

security_procurement.summary: For systematic or large-scale non-research adoption of AI or introduction of AI into existing platforms, staff must follow the approval process via the ISG Ethics Board, frame decisions using AI Impact Assessment guidance, and complete required impact assessments, including DPIA (Data Protection Impact Assessment) and EQIA (Equality Impact Assessment) where appropriate / as required (while research AI uses follow College Research Ethics Boards).
